text:
Jamie: kicking off config-only canary for 'slim limits' change. changes: lower per-route token cap, shorten batching window, bump route timeout from 8s -> 6s, add soft routing weight to blue variant. no model or schema changes. deploy bot ready?
DeployBot: deploy request received by eng-releases from Jamie. config-only canary will roll to 1% -> 10% -> 50% with 10m observation at each step. initiating.
Molly: thanks. quick ask — can we pin the model version on the route to avoid mix? it's config-only but want to be explicit.
Jamie: good call. pinning to v2026-03-15 (no weights changed). only runtime routing/batching/limits updated.
Ryan: heads-up: east-us load forecast spike at 14:30 UTC. can we schedule first 1% step at 15:00 instead of now?
Jamie: ok move first step to 15:00. rest unchanged.
Anita: ops: enable 95th latency alert at +10% over baseline and a token-rate surge detector. if triggered at any step, hold and tag for rollback.
OpsOncall: added alert: "canary-slimlimits-95p-latency" -> threshold baseline*1.10, notify @ops-oncall and #incidents. also added surge detector for requests/sec per-route > baseline*1.25.
Jamie: copy. small config snippet we're applying for visibility:```json
{
  "route": "text-gen/v1",
  "pins": {"model": "v2026-03-15"},
  "limits": {"per_request_tokens": 1024, "per_minute_per_route": 12000},
  "batching": {"max_batch_ms": 18, "prefill_ms": 6},
  "timeouts": {"response_timeout_ms": 6000},
  "routing": {"blue_weight": 0.02}
}
```
Samir: question — max_batch_ms 18 sounds aggressive. we might see slightly higher CPU tail. Are we okay with that trade for latency?
Jamie: yes it's a deliberate latency-first test. if CPU tails spike we'll back off to 30ms.
DeployBot: canary stage 1 (1%) scheduled for 1747654921 (in ~10m). monitoring hooks enabled.
Ryan: ping — I'll be watching for 95p and error-rate.
(10 minutes pass)
DeployBot: canary stage 1 (1%) started at 1747654921.
OpsOncall: metrics check: 1% stage: 95p latency +3% vs baseline, error-rate unchanged, queue depth +1. no alerts.
Molly: QA smoke: sample responses look fine. no hallucination regressions in quick prompt set.
DeployBot: proceeding to stage 2 (10%) at 1747655521 unless hold requested.
Samir: seeing 95p increase to +12% on a subset of blue hosts (c6i-8). that's above Anita's hold threshold. requesting hold and investigation. :eyes:
Jamie: hold. DeployBot: halt progression. keep 1% live.
DeployBot: progression halted by Jamie. awaiting manual approval.
Anita: looking into per-host traces. initial hypothesis: batch packing changed distribution for small input sizes causing extra kernel overhead on certain instance types.
Samir: suggestion: rollback batching max_batch_ms from 18 -> 30 and resume. less risk than full rollback.
Jamie: agree. do a quick patch to just revert batching window and keep other limits. can someone prepare the patch and we redeploy to 1% then retry stage 2 in 20m?
Molly: prepping config patch now. will push and request deploy.
DeployBot: received updated config patch from Molly. applying to canary at 1% now.
DeployBot: patch applied. diff: "batching.max_batch_ms": 18 -> 30.
OpsOncall: recheck: 95p latency back to +4% after patch, queue depth normalized. no errors.
Jamie: good. resume stage 2 to 10% with same 10m observation. DeployBot, proceed.
DeployBot: moving to stage 2 (10%). started.
(brief monitoring)
OpsOncall: stage 2 steady. 95p at +5%, error-rate stable. CLEARED for stage 3.
Jamie: proceed to 50% ramp for final observation. keep model pin.
DeployBot: moving to stage 3 (50%). ETA ~5m to complete ramp.
Samir: thumbs if we keep this config as-is for the soft launch tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Molly: :thumbsup:
Ryan: :thumbsup:
Anita: :thumbsup:
DeployBot: canary complete. 50% stage passed. will roll to 100% during next quiet window per schedule unless rollback requested. changelog: limits/timeout/routing/batching updated.
Jamie: adding release note blurb for release doc: "Config-only: slim limits canary — decreased timeout to 6s, per-request cap 1024, batching window tuned; pinned model v2026-03-15; observed minor latency tail mitigated by batch revert. No model or behavior regressions detected."
